reason: The cited evidence shows Hf can be incorporated into a similar W-Ta-Cr-V alloy (E1) and that Cr/V-rich precipitates form under thermal annealing in a related alloy (E2), but neither passage provides direct evidence that Hf segregates to grain boundaries, retards Cr/V diffusion, or suppresses radiation-induced precipitation. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: Hf segregates to grain boundaries in W-based refractory high-entropy alloys
Hf segregation at grain boundaries retards Cr and V diffusion along grain boundaries
Retarding Cr/V diffusion suppresses radiation-induced Cr/V precipitation
Grain boundaries in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 foster Cr/V segregation and precipitation
The unmodified alloy shows considerable radiation-induced Cr/V precipitation at ~8 dpa
